title: The hearing
summary: The fixer who texted you is in front of the league. They want you as a witness, in a room in London with a long table, and his lawyer is going to say you were in on it. The gaffer will drive you.

ends.title: The truth told
ends.text: You gave evidence at the fixer's hearing and his lawyer couldn't move you. He got eight years.

ends.title: The bad day
ends.text: You gave evidence at the fixer's hearing and his lawyer made a mess of you. He got four years, and the papers asked about you for a month.

beats.title: The long table

event.title: The long table
event.speaker: manager
setup: A room in London with a long table and water jugs nobody touches. The man who texted you is at the far end in a suit that doesn't fit him. His lawyer smiles at you like you're old friends.

say: The gaffer drove you down at five. In the corridor he says, "Just say what happened. Slow. He wants you to rush."
The lawyer: "You kept the number live for three weeks. Why would an innocent man do that?"

replies.label: Answer fast, to get it over.

slow.text: Forty minutes. The lawyer gets nothing. The gaffer buys you a pasty at the services and doesn't say a word all the way home, in a good way.

angry.text: It's true, and it's on the record, and the papers lead with you shouting.

rush.text: You get two dates wrong. The lawyer is very polite about it. You feel sick on the train.

beats.hint: The league want you as a witness

event.title: The verdict
event.speaker: manager
setup: A season on. The league's verdict is on every phone in the dressing room.

outcomes.text: Eight years. Your evidence is in paragraph four, and nobody could move it.
Four years. Paragraph four says a witness was "confused". You read it six times.
The gaffer reads it for you and says, "Eight. Good lad."
The lads tell you it was four, and don't look at you while they do.
